sentences.text:
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.33945 Of 2023
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed for issuance of writ of mandamus to declare the inaction of respondents in closing the temporary nala that was excavated on the private patta lands of the petitioners to tackle the surplus rain water coming out of Kotha Cheruvu and lead the flow into Tummalakunta Cheruvu while the process of approval for the construction of permanent drain network duly avoiding private lands was in progress, which was undertaken pursuant to intimation No.G1/1206/ 2022 dated 18.05.2022, as being illegal, arbitrary, breach of trust, trespass and inducement of false promises,
colourable exercise of powers and violative of Articles 19 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

2. Heard learned Counsel appearing on behalf of petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration & Urban Development for respondent No.1,3, 4, 9 and 10, Sri B. Jagan Madhav Rao, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.5 and 6, learned Government Pleader for Irrigation for respondent Nos.7 and 8 and with the consent of the learned Counsel appearing for the parties, the Writ Petition is taken up for hearing and disposal at the stage of admission.
3.

Petitioners contend that during the year 2022, the respondent authorities in order to address the surplus water flowing from Kotha Cheruvu into Tummalakunta Cheruvu had dug a channel/nala through the petitioners' patta land as a temporary measure to drain out the surplus water; and that inspite of monsoon season of 2022 having passed by, the respondent authorities have not taken steps to close the temporary nala which was dug through the petitioners' land; and that the respondent authorities are not heeding to the request of the petitioners even allowing them to close the said nala dug through their private patta lands.

4. Petitioners further contend that the respondents who undertook the aforesaid excavation in the name of temporary nala to address the flow of surplus water during rainy season of the year 2022 or indirectly making it as a permanent nala, without following due process of law.
5. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners in support of the aforesaid contention of the said excavation is being temporary in nature has referred to the proceedings dated 18.05.2022.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.5 and 6 has placed before this Court the written instructions titled as 'Brief facts on behalf of respondent No.5' under the signature of respondent No.5.

By the aforesaid written instructions, the respondent No.5 do not dispute the fact that the authorities having undertaken the excavation work through the private patta lands for the flow of surplus water from Kotha Cheruvu to Tummalakunta Cheruvu.

7. By the aforesaid instructions, the respondent No.5 further states that in the month of April, 2022,
a katcha nala was dug parallel to the existing nala, which was dug through the petitioners' land and that the intention of digging the katcha nala parallel to the nala dug during the year 2023 was to check whether the storm water discharge is freely flowing and reaching the point where the water touches 60 feet Master plan road.
8. By the aforesaid written instructions, it is further stated that out of the total extent of katcha nala that was dug through the petitioners land was about 1500 square metres.

After cross checking free flow of water through the newly dug kutch nala, the land of petitioners to an extent of 625 square metres would get affected and that the authorities are required to take steps for acquiring the same.
By the said written instructions, it is also stated that the land acquisition process has been initiated.

9. Having regard to the submission made as above, this Court had called upon the learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.5 to place before this Court the land acquisition proceedings stated to have been initiated for acquiring the land of the petitioners as claimed.

On the aforesaid query being made by this Court, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.5 has placed before this Court the Form-I addressed by the respondent No.5 to the respondent Nos.3 and 4 requesting to acquire land of the petitioner to an extent of 750 square yards in Sy. No.1524 for formation of katcha nala to access water from Kotha Cheruvu tank.

Though the aforesaid Form I under which a request is made by the respondent No.5 to the respondent Nos.3 and 4, the same does not bear any date and bears only the initials as having received on 05.12.2023

,
it is not clear as to who has received the aforesaid communication stated to have been addressed by the respondent No.5 for initiating acquisition proceedings.

10. Be that as it may, since, the respondent No.5 by their written instructions have stated initiation of land acquisition proceedings as per Form - I as placed before this Court showing initiation of acquisition proceedings to acquire the land of the petitioner to an extent of 750 square yards, this Court is of the view that the petitioner cannot be deprived of use of the remaining land to an extent of 774 square yards.

Since, the respondent authorities have now stated to have initiated acquisition proceedings in respect of land admeasuring 750 square yards, the respondents are required to bring back the remaining land to normal position as it is existed prior to the respondent authorities taking up excavation work in the year April, 2022 by closing the nala excavated thereon within a period o 11.

In so far as the land that is stated to be required by the respondents, for which proceedings to acquire the same are stated to have been initiated, the authorities shall take steps to complete the acquisition of the aforesaid land as per the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in an expeditious manner.
